title: Rank findings by their effect on learners
statement: Rank findings by effect on learners: anything that can mislead, falsely reject, block or wrongly advance a learner holds the work, polish comes last, and preferences aren't defects.
detail: The Grade 5 instruction-review profile ranks findings by what they do to learners (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/courses/g5-reading/review/generated/instruction-review-profile.json`, lines 129-133). Its top priority blocks bounded review because a learner can be misled, falsely rejected, unable to complete the intended work or given invalid progression; the next must be corrected before external submission because instruction, feedback or transfer is materially weaker than the intended design; presentation polish comes last and cannot override either.

evidence.quote: Blocks bounded review because a learner can be misled, falsely rejected, unable to complete the intended work, or given invalid progression.
Must be corrected before external submission because instruction, feedback, or transfer is materially weaker than the intended learning design.
Presentation polish required before production; it cannot override a P0 or P1 student-outcome requirement.
Tier 1: semantic student-task validity, truthful gate/score meaning and complete evidence.
Tier 2: consistency, readable layout, keyboard flow, recoverable errors
Use P0 for blocked completion, P1 for a materially confusing/broken task, P2 for a usable but harmful inconsistency, P3 for an optional refinement.
Do not inflate a subjective preference into a defect.
